The subject is the HTM ACL balance history.

comparisons.peer_topic: Allowance for Credit Losses on Investment Securities Balances
comparisons.peer_summary: The allowance for credit losses on investment securities was $152 million, $128 million, and $96 million as of December 31, 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively. This amount included a cumulative-effect adjustment to retained earnings related to the transfer of held-to-maturity (HTM) securities to available-for-sale (AFS) for the year ended December 31, 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup (C) and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) report the dollar amount of their allowance for credit losses on investment securities. C reports an allowance of $137 million as of Dec 31, 2024, while JPM reports $152 million for the same date. JPM specifically notes that its 2023 figure included a cumulative-effect adjustment related to transferring HTM securities to AFS, a detail not explicitly quantified as a separate adjustment in C's 2024 summary, though both track similar asset classes.

sentences.text: The allowance for credit losses on HTM debt securities, which the Company has the intent and ability to hold, was $137 million, $95 million and $120 million as of December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, respectively.

The allowance for credit losses on investment securities was $152 million, $128 million and $96 million as of December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, respectively, which included a cumulative-effect adjustment to retained earnings related to the transfer of HTM securities to AFS for the year ended December 31, 2023.

comparisons.peer_topic: HTM Securities Allowance for Credit Losses
comparisons.peer_summary: Held-to-Maturity securities carried net amounts reflecting an allowance for credit losses of $52 million as of December 31, 2024 and $44 million as of December 31, 2023, predominantly related to Non-agency CMBS.
comparisons.comparison: Morgan Stanley (MS) and Citigroup (C) both disclose the specific dollar value of the allowance for credit losses on Held-to-Maturity (HTM) securities. MS reports an ACL of $52 million as of Dec 31, 2024, which is notably lower than C's $137 million. Both companies' disclosures imply these amounts are netted against the carrying value or represent the specific reserve held for expected losses on these specific securities.
